- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon when sentiment is strongly bullish (positive sentiment > 0.5) — model tends to overshoot upward momentum.
- Underestimate when sentiment is strongly bearish (negative sentiment < -0.5) — model fails to capture downward pressure or panic.
- Lag in reaction to recent sentiment shifts — model often takes 2–3 days to adjust after sentiment flips.
- Overshoot after sharp spikes — model overreacts to recent highs, especially if sentiment was bullish but then turned neutral or bearish.
- Mean reversion bias — model tends to overcorrect after strong moves, especially in the 10–15 day window.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are consistently too low in the first 5–7 days, then rise sharply — model underestimates early volatility and overestimates late recovery.
- Sentiment-weighted correction: if sentiment is > 0.7, add 5–10% to forecast; if < -0.7, subtract 5–10% — model ignores sentiment strength in calibration.
